jane_cust: Hi all — since yesterday afternoon our rerank calls have been getting 429s and some responses are empty or have weird scores. Noticed it spikes when we send large candidate arrays (~500).

amy_support: Sorry you're hitting this, Jane. Can you paste a minimal repro payload + the request_id from headers when you see a 429? Also which region are you hitting?

jane_cust: payload looks like:```json
{
  "query": "Find the best docs about auth",
  "candidates": ["doc1","doc2", ..., "doc500"],
  "top_n": 5
}
```
Headers included `x-request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d` and response had `status: 429`, body `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"rate limit exceeded"}`. Region: us-east-1.

amy_support: Thanks — 429 + rate_limited typically means the rerank quota/rate window was hit. Two quick workarounds while we investigate: 1) send candidates in smaller batches (<= 100) 2) implement exponential backoff reading `Retry-After` header. Can you try batching and see if it helps?

jane_cust: batching to 100 does reduce 429s but latency is higher overall. We also see occasional unexpected scores (very low variance) for some requests even when they succeed.

ravi_oncall: tagging infra. From logs for rq_0a1b2c3d I see a burst around 2026-03-16T18:12:34Z: rerank shard quota exhausted -> returning 429. There's also a follow-up 502 from the downstream scoring service for some candidate sets which could lead to fallthrough results with low scores.

amy_support: @ravi_oncall can you confirm whether rerank requests share a token bucket with other endpoints? Customer suspects rerank-specific throttling.

ravi_oncall: Quick summary: current implementation uses a shared regional token bucket for all scoring/rerank traffic to protect the scoring cluster. We do apply soft limits per-customer but the global bucket can be consumed by embedding + batch-encode jobs. In this incident embedding job spikes earlier correlated with the 429 window.

tom_support_mgr: We should not leave customers without a mitigation. Suggestion: 1) grant a temporary per-customer quota bump for jane_cust org ID (org_7654) for 24h, 2) update docs to call out recommended max candidates and batching pattern, 3) add telemetry to distinguish rerank vs embed consumption in the global bucket.

ravi_oncall: Agreed. I've opened infra ticket INFRA-9142 to add a dedicated rerank subnet quota and a short-term quota override for org_7654. Also creating a replay task to reproduce with large candidate arrays.

amy_support: Jane — we created SUPPORT-12345 and requested a 24h quota override. ETA ~4 hours for the override to propagate. In the meantime please do the 100-candidate batching and add Retry-After backoff. If you want, we can schedule a short call to walk through your traffic pattern.

jane_cust: Thanks. One more question — can you confirm if negative or NaN scores we've seen are related to the 429s? We got a couple responses like `scores: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]` when normally there is variance.

ravi_oncall: The 0.0/flat scores look like a fallback path: when the scoring backend responds slowly or returns an error, the reranker falls back to a simple heuristic (uniform scoring) to avoid blocking. That explains empty/flat scores during partial failures. We'll log that path more clearly and return a `warning` field in the response in future to signal degraded quality.

amy_support: For repro steps we asked infra to run this script (pseudo):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/rerank \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"query":"q","candidates":["a"..."z" /* 500 items */],"top_n":5}' &
done
```
This will reproduce the burst and should trigger the shared bucket fast.

tom_support_mgr: Action items: (amy) keep customer updated, (ravi) infra to apply override + follow up with dedicated limit design, (eng-runtime) investigate fallback scoring path and improve diagnostics.

amy_support: Noted. Jane — we'll follow up here once override is applied. Ping me if 429s continue after batching. :thumbsup:

jane_cust: Appreciate it. I'll try batching and report back.
